rows.title: In-Tank Fuel Pump Failure

rows.title: Power Steering Pressure Line Leak
rows.howToFix: Replace the high-pressure power steering line assembly. Flush the system with fresh power steering fluid after replacement. Inspect the power steering pump for damage from running low on fluid — a whining pump indicates internal damage. Fill and bleed the system by turning the wheel lock-to-lock several times.

rows.howToFix: Replace the corroded rear A/C lines. Aftermarket stainless steel replacement lines are available and resist future corrosion. Evacuate and recharge the entire A/C system after repair. Apply undercoating to the new lines for corrosion protection. Some owners delete the rear A/C system entirely and cap the lines.

rows.title: Power Sliding Door Motor and Cable Failure
rows.howToFix: Inspect the power sliding door for frayed or broken drive cables, a weak/burned-out motor, worn center roller, and latch/track binding before replacing parts; also check the door module fuse, wiring at the door harness, and verify the latch and track move freely by hand with the power function disabled. On these Venture vans, the usual repair is replacement of the sliding door motor/cable assembly and any damaged rollers or latch components, followed by cleaning/lubricating the upper, center, and lower tracks and performing a door relearn/calibration if applicable. If the cable has wrapped or jammed in the drum, do not keep cycling the door, as it can damage the regulator and rear latch. Typical repair cost is about $400-$900 depending on whether an aftermarket cable kit or complete OEM-style motor/regulator assembly is used, with higher costs if latch or track hardware also needs replacement.
